The champion (score -11.73) is dramatically better than everything else. Let me analyze what it does:
- State 0: Exploration (B=0, rwm=70) with LED cyan, transitions when neighbors < 2 (condition 4) → goes to state 1
- State 1: GoAwayColor (B=9, clr=2=green) with LED off, transitions on BLACK floor (p=0.979) → state 0, or on GRAY floor (p=0.5288) → state 0

This is interesting: the robot explores, and when it has few neighbors (isolated), it goes to GoAwayColor from GREEN. When on black floor (source area) or gray, it returns to exploration. This effectively makes robots go to the source area by avoiding green walls, pick up items (from the non-green half, presumably blue), then return.

Wait - GoAwayColor from GREEN (clr=2) means moving away from green walls. The source has BLUE walls on one half and GREEN on the other. Moving away from green would push toward the blue half. The robot enters the blue half (black floor), picks up a blue item, then transitions back to exploration on black/gray floor.

The key insight: items from one half decrease score by 1 (good), from the other increase by 1 (bad). The champion avoids GREEN, so it goes to the BLUE half. Blue items decrease score → good.

4. Try GoToColor with RED (clr=1) to navigate back to nest, combined with blue-avoiding or green-avoiding logic
